The further out in time, the more factors come into play, making precise prediction more difficult and expanding the probable range of results.

While the confidence intervals capture a wide range of probable outcomes, certain high-impact events could push the actual results outside these bounds. On the upside, an unexpected breakthrough innovation, a sudden surge in market demand, or a major positive policy change could lead to significantly higher outcomes than predicted. Conversely, severe economic downturns, unforeseen supply chain disruptions, a major operational failure (such as a significant data breach or a natural disaster impacting key facilities), or intense negative publicity could cause results to fall well below the lower end of our forecast. These extreme scenarios, while less probable, represent significant external or internal shocks that are not fully captured within the typical range of variability expected by our statistical model.
